title: Russian Barrage Hits NATO Territory as Moscow Unleashes Massive Attack Across Ukraine
snippet: Russia launched over 80 missiles and 400 drones across Ukraine in a massive overnight assault that spilled into Poland, prompting Warsaw to accuse Moscow of a deliberate provocation.
content:
Moscow unleashed one of its most devastating aerial assaults of the war overnight, pounding cities across Ukraine with a barrage of more than 80 missiles and 400 drones while spilling into NATO territory, officials said Friday.

The massive assault left at least six people dead and 15 injured in Kyiv, with two additional fatalities reported in the western city of Lviv. The strikes dealt a severe blow to Ukraine's civilian infrastructure, causing widespread blackouts across ten regions and leaving the Black Sea port city of Odesa in critical condition. In the capital, three vital transport bridges crossing the Dnipro River were targeted, threatening further severe disruption to daily life.

NATO Tensions Surge After Munitions Land in Poland

The bombardment sparked an immediate international crisis after Polish authorities confirmed that a Russian missile landed in the eastern village of Nowy Lipowiec, with another missile and a jet-powered drone suspected of hitting two other locations in the country's southeast corner. While no casualties were reported in Poland, Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk declared the incident an intentional act of aggression.

"The provocation may have been linked with the fact that there are military exercises taking place on the territory of Poland," Tusk said during a televised address in Warsaw, referring to drills involving thousands of European troops. "Nobody can say that this was an innocent coincidence."

Tusk confirmed he immediately contacted NATO leadership, adding that NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte is set to arrive in Warsaw on Saturday for emergency consultations.

Retaliation Follows High-Stakes Diplomacy

The sudden escalation comes just hours after Russian President Vladimir Putin met with Chinese President Xi Jinping and U.S. President Donald Trump at a summit in China. During the trip, Putin pledged a "painful" response to recent Ukrainian strikes targeting the strategic Kerch Bridge in Crimea.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky condemned the overnight campaign as one of Moscow's largest barrages since the full-scale invasion began nearly five years ago. Speaking after meetings with European allies in Berlin, Zelensky denounced the strikes as Russian "terror" and dismissed Putin's diplomatic efforts to reshape international order alongside Beijing and Washington as a failure.

Following the attacks, France called for an emergency meeting of the United Nations Security Council, declaring that Russia must answer for its actions. Meanwhile, humanitarian organizations warned of the war's mounting human cost. UNICEF reported Friday that at least 114 children have been killed and over 1,000 injured in Ukraine through the first ten months of 2026—marking a sharp rise in child casualties compared to previous years of the conflict.
